role: Source-backed question author; not independent coverage or key-scope auditor.
scope: Original FFG English 2008 CE01 default base rules, original fifty aliens, applicable base card/flare FAQ; exclude optional Technology/all variants, expansions and Anniversary extras.
seed_novelty_method: Compare proposed required facts with the actual seed question clauses, not merely extra facts present in its answer key. Cross-alien examples with no new procedure should be merged or omitted.

candidates.label: Cosmic Quake and base Aftershock

accepted_passages_without_an_explicit_se.ruling_summary: If a required cosmic-deck draw cannot be made because both deck and discard are empty, everyone discards and is dealt eight after reshuffling (Cosmic Quake). If insufficient, Cosmic Aftershock discards all cosmic cards including Miser's hoard; setup card holdings are replenished. Omit expansion reward cards, Cryo, Cyborg and The Claw.
If Quake is insufficient, discard and reshuffle all cards; redeal setup holdings such as Miser's hoard.
Compensation requires ships actually lost to the warp; Zombie prevention and Void eradication do not qualify.

Lost ships go to the warp involuntarily; losing ships are those involved that should go there; sent ships result from specific actions and count as lost. Observer covers all three; Void eradicates losing ships. Expansion-specific Fungus/Remote behavior is excluded.
Ships prevented from reaching the warp are not lost/sent to it; Healer cannot heal Zombie ships that never arrive. Ghoul/capture examples are excluded.
Reclaiming an empty home planet is a win and a successful encounter.
Cards may be legally played before compensation starts, but hand-targeting effects cannot then be interrupted except by Zaps/explicit interrupts. Hacker's target is too late to dump reinforcements.
Winning and making a deal are successful encounters; a deal is not a win for effects such as Cudgel or Barbarian. Guerrilla example excluded.
Mobius Tubes releases ships; those without a colony return to the warp, except the offense can first place up to four in the gate.
Start Turn occurs only on the first encounter, before Regroup effects; offense draws a new hand before a Regroup Plague.
When order matters, discard non-encounter cards alphabetically/numerically first, then encounter cards from offense clockwise with defense last/top. Expansion Omni-Zap/Cavalry examples excluded.
The FAQ gives no official two-player variant.
Automatically reclaiming an empty home planet proceeds only through Launch.
A required sacrifice from outside the encounter cannot be paid with an involved ship.
If no ships exist outside the encounter when such losses are required, lose none.
An encounter continues with no offensive ships; victory gives no foreign colony unless an effect specifically permits it.
Hand contents may be claimed or lied about, but cards cannot be shown absent an effect; Mind has its own speech restrictions.
Modified values determine encounter totals; a card's printed identity governs other targeting effects. Morph remains a Morph by identity. Expansion examples excluded.
Encounter-resolution effects use the current modified card type/value; other effects use the printed type/value. Expansion-specific The Claw behavior excluded.
Morph copying an attack is treated as that attack for encounter totals; do not import The Claw.
Simultaneously discarded faceup cards may all be inspected, absent a contrary power.
Changing a negotiate into attack 42 with Human Wild does not satisfy Cudgel's requirement of originally revealing an attack. Brute/Deuce excluded.
A player who loses a power is no longer considered that alien.
Fodder and Reserve choose all cards for one power use together, rather than repeated selections. Porcupine excluded.
An explicitly immediate win ends the game when its effect resolves unless zapped or explicitly interrupted. The Glutton flare itself is excluded.
If offense already has colonies on every planet in the defensive system, redraw destiny.
Discard piles are public unless an effect says otherwise.
Hand size must be disclosed unless an effect allows secrecy.
Table talk must be public unless an effect says otherwise.
Defensive allies count as in the hyperspace gate for effect terminology.
Unless otherwise specified, forced ship loss/sacrifice/transfer chooses a ship under your control. The researching-Tech example is excluded with the Technology variant.
Plague requires one held card of each actual type, including Morph; the extra rift/kicker/retreat/intimidate types and variable attacks are excluded from the original set.
Remove the alien with the printed incompatibility; its player may use their rejected alien or draw a replacement flare, redrawing conflicts.
Absent contrary text, the player losing extra ships chooses which ships. Gambler applies; Skeptic excluded.
A legal encounter can ultimately yield a foreign colony without requiring a deal.
Powers are usable once per relevant context unless specified otherwise, e.g. Hate once per turn and Vulch each qualifying artifact discard.
A player may reconsider an invoked optional effect if another action/timing changes the state. Trader example generalizes; Visionary excluded.
Deal colonies coexist; do not vacate a colony when granting one. Grant only where you currently have a colony, including a foreign colony.
A one-sided deal is valid if at least one card or colony changes hands.
Tangible deal terms are limited to permitted cards/one colony and explicit power/card exceptions. At least one card or colony must change hands; promises are allowed but unenforceable.
Card/colony deal terms may be vague or specific, but cannot be lied about and must be fulfilled.
A canceled flare counts against the player's one-flare limit if the flare itself was targeted.
When an effect specifies ship number, each Macron ship counts as one, including Virus flares. Fungus excluded.
If zapped, use your own flare as Wild and keep it after resolution rather than giving it to yourself/discarding it as if your alien were absent.
An actual power use enabled by a Super flare may be Cosmic Zapped.
Power use remains zappable even when Super changes its usual phase.
Cosmic Zap of Super-enabled power neither discards the flare nor forces immediate Wild play; it stays in hand and Wild is available while zapped.

Zap may follow the immediate revealed effect (Chosen draws; Philanthropist's given card), but only in the short same-phase window before later actions; no retroactive Zap after reinforcements change the outcome. Seeker excluded.
A Start Turn Zap lasts throughout the current encounter.
Amoeba moves all chosen ships simultaneously and may ooze all twenty before power loss from stripping home colonies occurs.
Amoeba that Super-oozes all ships away as an ally still counts as having allied.
Amoeba Wild can increase a defense ship count of zero.
A flare prevented by Anti-Matter remains in hand, does not spend its player's flare limit, and cannot be attempted again that encounter.
Anti-Matter Super must be played anew each encounter it is used.
Chosen Super is played after inspecting drawn cards.
Chosen may be Zapped after drawing and showing its intended card.
Citadels remain when Citadel's sheet is facedown, but are discarded when the sheet is discarded.
After Sorcerer switching, Clone keeps the card ending before Clone; Filch takes the card ending before the opponent.
Clone keeps first; Filch versus Fido follows normal timing.
Clone Super permits any compensation amount from normal to double.
Mind cannot inspect Miser's hoard. Cryo and AI are excluded.
Cudgel Super must be played for each encounter in which its effect is desired.
Fido takes actual played encounter cards, not cards discarded by Plague, Fodder or Reserve; Deuce's extra card is an excluded example.
Clone keeps first; Filch versus Fido follows normal timing.
Clone keeps first; Filch versus Fido follows normal timing.
After Sorcerer switching, Clone keeps its final card; Filch takes the opponent's final card.
Classic Filch flare remains unrevealed until caught cheating, at which point it can be zapped.
Filch cannot take Gambler's unrevealed card: it goes beneath the deck instead of being discarded. Any reference to reward-deck destination is excluded.
Fodder Wild may join only a side that originally invited the player that encounter.
Fodder Super allows discarding attacks below the opponent's card regardless of Fodder's own value, not attacks above the opponent.
Gambler/Sorcerer restriction prevents a disclosed-card bluff; FAQ permits using both if players accept that issue.
Gambler must reveal or bluff before Oracle chooses a card.
An ally initially committing at least one ship to Grudge avoids its token even if ships later leave, including through Amoeba or Force Field.
Hate can discard Morph, forcing others to discard Morph or lose ships. Special Crooked Deal cards are excluded.
Hate can be Zapped after choosing its discard and then keeps that card.
Offensive Hate draws a necessary new hand before using its power.
Against Hate's attack 20, a player without a higher attack they wish to discard discards nothing and loses three ships; a lower attack cannot be discarded.
Healer returns ships after they have actually reached the warp, permitting Remora retrieval triggers.
Healer cannot heal Zombie ships prevented from reaching the warp.
Vacuum triggers on actual warp loss before healing; Healer can then heal Vacuum's and other eligible non-Healer ships.
Human/Pacifist conflicting wins resolve by normal timing: the first effect wins.
Human can be zapped to win even with one or both negotiates revealed.
Human's opponent gets compensation after Human's zap win only if Human actually revealed an attack.
Human Super can add eight and then be discarded to zap, or be discarded solely for zap without adding eight.
Kamikaze chooses and sacrifices all ships for one power use together before drawing cards.
Kamikaze Super must be played anew for each encounter it is used.
Machine Wild guarantees a second encounter and a new hand if needed: play flare, discard old hand, draw, then return flare to hand.
Machine Super must be played anew each encounter it is used.
Machine Wild must be played each time its second-encounter effect is desired.
Macron can be zapped at launch to allow up to four ordinary ships, or after reveal to remove its four-per-ship value.
Macron Super's up-to-four ships also applies when defending as an ally.
Masochist Super must be played anew each encounter it is used.
Mind cannot inspect Miser's hoard; Cryo storage is excluded.
Mind Wild is played anew for each encounter in which desired, and its effect then lasts through that encounter.
A flare played from Miser's hoard returns to that hoard.
An encounter card only in Miser's hoard does not authorize a second encounter.
Any card returning to hand goes back to the hoard if played from it.
Mind cannot inspect Miser's hoard; Cryo storage is excluded.
Miser may pay any required hand discard, including Hate, from the hoard instead.
Miser Super must be played anew each encounter it is used.
Miser Wild can save fewer than two cards.

Observer's Resolution protection covers all its ships as ally and all allies' ships as main player, including remote losses. It can relocate protected Grudge losses and use Void Wild without paying a ship loss; it does not extend protection outside Resolution.
Observer does not protect against Void eradication.
Gambler must reveal or bluff before Oracle chooses its card.
Pacifist forced to negotiate by Loser gets compensation only if Loser revealed an attack.
Human/Pacifist conflicting wins resolve by normal timing, first effect winning.
Philanthropist Super requires defense to play the given card; defense cannot use general timing to evade that effect.
Philanthropist Wild loan includes associated holdings such as Miser's hoard; Fury's expansion tokens are excluded.
Reincarnator flare occurs after the end of the encounter, allowing same-phase power use beforehand.
Reincarnator Wild cannot target oneself because it specifies another player.
Reincarnator cannot use incarnation aliens' Super flares.
Zapped Reserve keeps the attack card it was about to play.
Reserve Wild is played once and may collect every eligible discarded reinforcement for the rest of the encounter.
Shadow executes for each destiny card drawn, not only the final used card.
After Sorcerer, Clone keeps its final card and Filch takes the opponent's final card.
FAQ allows Gambler/Sorcerer together if players accept that Sorcerer's prior knowledge undermines the bluff restriction.
Defensive Trader with no cards must draw a new hand before trading; it cannot trade an empty hand.
Vacuum cannot target itself.
Vacuum Super losses are simultaneous and can remove all one-ship Zombie foreign colonies; Zombie cannot move saved ships to another colony being lost in that effect.
Vacuum's warp loss triggers before healing; Healer may heal it and other affected non-Healer ships afterward.
Virus Wild with no allies multiplies by zero.
Void does not eradicate failed-deal losses; it must win as main player, or as ally with Super.
Losing a negotiate to Void yields no compensation because ships never go to the warp.
Void eradication precedes/precludes Zombie prevention and Observer protection.
Vulch cannot collect the Cosmic Zap that zapped it because the power is unavailable when the Zap is discarded.
Vulch can take artifacts discarded by the player using Vulch Wild against it, potentially handing them back repeatedly.
Vulch Super lasts for all eligible flare discards in the encounter; play on the first such discard. It cannot retrieve itself.
Warpish counts ships added to the warp before its use, not afterward; apply timing rules if needed.
Warrior continues earning experience when Zapped because that part does not require power use.
Warrior earns experience for reclaiming an empty home planet, which counts as a win.
Will cannot attack an absent colony on a third player's planet; a home owner can still defend an empty home planet.
Zombie gets compensation only if its ships actually reach the warp, e.g. while zapped; its ordinary prevention yields none.
Zombie deal liberation has no numerical limit.
Healer cannot heal Zombie ships that never reach the warp.
Zombie can invoke Kamikaze Wild and similar ship-to-warp costs, then use its power to prevent arrival.
Vacuum Super removes simultaneous Zombie colonies without letting saved ships relocate to another colony lost in the same effect.
Void eradicates Zombie's ships directly without sending them to the warp.
Zombie may free only its negotiating opponent's ships in the deal, not third-party Masochist's ships.
A player with no colonies or ships retrieves one ship at Regroup and may place it on any home planet. This specific FAQ instruction differs from rulebook's general no-colony placement into the gate.
Hacker compensation follows offense, defense, then non-main players clockwise. Reward-deck draw source itself is excluded.
